structured_output.summary: Closest CIFAR-100 precedent: the futurebiohackers PR #3 reached 75.29% in 8.11 s on A100 with an airbench port: patch-whitening, 3 conv groups, lookahead/EMA, alternating flip, compile+warmup in build, SGD. Its notes say Muon lost to SGD at every size and was dropped (seen via search snippets; the PR pages now return 404). That mean would just miss our 0.753 3-seed bar, so the ~1 s / ~1 epoch gap between E005 (0.7583 @ 9.10 s) and ~8.1 s is roughly where our margin runs out. Main differences from the references: airbench96_faster/airbench94 decay LR to exactly 0 (port ends at 0.07 of peak), and airbench96_faster uses LS 0.2, momentum 0.85, widths 128/384/512 (port 576), lookahead weight 0.95**5·(t/T)**3 every 5 steps with a full final copy, and whitening from 5k images. CIFAR-10 ablations: alternating flip without TTA ≈ 15% speedup at 10 epochs; whitening ≈ 2× speed; Dirac cut epochs 21→18; lookahead cut 13.5→12.0. Systems: Fable's 24/28/32 px progressive resizing (3 epochs each) saved ≈10% on CIFAR-10 and needed a global max-pool head; whole-run CUDA graphs beat per-step graphs by only ≈5 ms ('not launch-bound'); Fulcrum's audit flagged moving whitening/augmentation out of the timed region as gaming. Proxy-based data filtering's −21% came from a 45-epoch 96% run and is unproven at ~9 epochs.

findings.claim: CIFAR-100 speedrun submission adapted from airbench reached a 75.29% mean in 8.11 s on A100 (organizer ResNet9 baseline: 75.36% in 59.3 s). Recipe: patch-whitening stem, three conv groups, lookahead EMA, alternating flip, compile and warmup in the untimed build. Muon 'lost to SGD at every size' and was removed.
findings.relevance: Direct precedent on the same benchmark. Strong prior against H1.2/H1.2.1. Its 0.7529 mean would fail our 0.753 3-seed bar, so the time-optimal recipe sits at about 8.1-8.5 s for a similar net. E005 (0.7583 @ 9.10 s) has about 1 epoch to give back.

findings.claim: Reference hyperparameters: LR schedule warms up linearly from 0.2x to 1.0x over the first 10% of steps, then decays linearly to exactly 0. Nesterov momentum 0.85; lr 9.0 and wd 0.012 per 1024; BN-bias lr scaled 64x; label smoothing 0.2; widths 128/384/512. Lookahead every 5 steps with alpha = 0.95**5*(t/T)**3 and a final full copy (decay=1.0). Whitening from the first 5000 training images via eigendecomposition, eps 5e-4. Proxy net 32/64/64 at depth 2 keeps the top 512 of 1024 by loss.
findings.relevance: The port's LR ends at 0.07 of peak per the E005 post-mortem, while the reference decays to 0. Decay-to-zero is the cheapest test of the 'cut late-training noise' lesson. The reference's LS 0.2 and width 512 bear on H1.3.1 and on per-epoch cost. Whitening on 5k images is already the reference practice (H3.2.1).

findings.claim: Without TTA, alternating flip vs random flip gives a 15.0% speedup at 10 epochs, 27.1% at 20 and 38.3% at 40. With TTA the gains are smaller. Patch-whitening roughly doubled training speed (94% in 21 epochs); Dirac init cut that to 18 epochs. Lookahead cut epochs from 13.5 to 12.0 (5.1 s to 4.6 s). The triangular schedule decays to zero. airbench96 transfers to CIFAR-100: 79.27% without Cutout vs ResNet-18's 77.54%.
findings.relevance: Supports H1.4/H1.4.1 (a ~15% epoch-equivalent at 10 epochs is likely well over 0.3 pp) and H1.1.2 (whitening plus Dirac is worth several epochs). Shows the backbone works on CIFAR-100. The CIFAR-10 lookahead gain (~11% of epochs) is smaller than our CIFAR-100 gain, which fits the E005 post-mortem.

findings.claim: Muon setup: conv filters only; lr 0.24; momentum 0.6 (Nesterov); no weight decay on Muon params; weights renormalized each step; batch size 2000; 8 epochs; linear decay to 0. Whitening bias trains only for the first 3 epochs; other params use SGD (momentum 0.85, BN-bias lr 0.053, head lr 0.67). On CIFAR-10 it went from 3.09 s (compiled SGD) to 2.59 s, about 16%.
findings.relevance: Gives the exact config for H1.2.1 if it is tested at all. The CIFAR-10 gain does not appear to transfer to CIFAR-100 (see the PR #3 finding), so the prior should be lowered.

findings.claim: Progressive resizing at 3 epochs each of 24, 28 and 32 px over 9 epochs saved 0.128 s, plus 0.081 s more for the full three-tier version, on a run of about 2 s (≈10%). Relative cost: 24 px = 0.56x and 28 px = 0.77x of 32 px. MaxPool2d(3) had to become a global max pool because feature maps are 2x2 at 24 px; that change was neutral at 32 px (2.298 vs 2.283 s, n=200). One CUDA graph for the whole run was only ~5 ms better than per-step graphs ('not launch-bound'). The audit flagged moving whitening and augmentation outside the timed region as specification gaming.
findings.relevance: Supports H2.3/H2.3.1 being worth testing (≈10% on CIFAR-10; the extra epochs CIFAR-100 needs are unknown) and lists the architecture change it requires. Predicts small gains for H2.2.2. H3.2 savings must come from a faster prepare, not from moving work into build.

findings.claim: CIFAR-10 94% went from 2.59 s to 1.98 s (-23.6%) using a vectorised/batched optimizer, fully vectorised batch cropping, a compiled forward/backward step, GELU→SiLU, SVD whitening init, fp16 + channels_last, brightness/contrast augmentation, and retuned epochs/LR/momentum. Selective TTA was also used but is banned here. No per-technique breakdown.
findings.relevance: Supports H2.2 (E004 already got -14% from compile + fused SGD). SiLU and brightness/contrast augmentation are untested accuracy-per-epoch ideas.

findings.claim: An automated agent tuning airbench96 got a 4.59% wallclock cut (26.36 s to 25.15 s) by skipping validation, shortening the schedule, raising LR intensity, and using a faster warmup to repair the accuracy margin. 81 of 97 trials missed the accuracy gate.
findings.relevance: Near the bar, epoch cuts need re-tuned LR/warmup to hold accuracy, and most tuning attempts fall below the gate. Supports treating margin and noise as the binding constraint. A faster warmup is an untested lever.

findings.claim: Proxy-model data filtering (backprop on the top 50% by proxy loss) took 96% CIFAR-10 from 34.7 s to 27.3 s (-21%), but in a 45-epoch, high-accuracy regime.
findings.relevance: No evidence it helps in ~9-epoch, under-trained CIFAR-100 runs, where the epoch budget, not easy-example redundancy, is the limit. Keep H2.4 low priority.

findings.claim: After weight averaging (SWA/EMA) with BatchNorm, PyTorch recommends recomputing BN statistics (update_bn) or also averaging the buffers. It says updating normalization statistics has empirically been shown to increase accuracy.
findings.relevance: Untested follow-up to E005: BN recalibration of the averaged weights, which must run inside timed train. Only worth it if the cost (one forward pass over a subset) is below the accuracy-equivalent epochs it saves.
